title: Index Prefix
statement: Implement `solve(columns, filters, order_by)`. `columns` is the composite index, left to right. `filters` is the list of equality columns in the query, in index order. `order_by` is a column name or an empty string. Return `yes` when `filters` is a prefix of `columns` and `order_by` is either empty or the next column in the index. Return `no` otherwise.
constraints: Equality columns must be the leading prefix
The sort can use the next column
hints: Then the next column may match order_by.
A filter that skips a leading column is no.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A composite index serves a leftmost prefix.

editorial: A composite index serves a leftmost prefix. Equality on the leading columns, then a sort on the following column, can walk the index in order. Filtering only on a later column cannot. This function is that rule for one index and one query shape.
